card.title: Central dogma — DNA to protein, one-way street

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: DNA's double helix (Watson-Crick, 1953) stores heredity: antiparallel strands, deoxyribose sugar, A=T (2 H-bonds) and G≡C (3 H-bonds), complementary base pairing enabling faithful replication. Semiconservative replication (Meselson-Stahl) unwinds and copies each strand; transcription makes mRNA from the template; translation decodes mRNA in 3-base codons into amino acids via the genetic code (64 codons, 20 amino acids, AUG start, UAA/UAG/UGA stop). Gene regulation (lac operon: repressor + operator + promoter) switches genes on/off.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: DNA: A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds) · replication: semiconservative (each daughter = old strand + new strand) · genetic code: 64 codons → 20 amino acids · AUG = start (Met) · stops: UAA, UAG, UGA · lac operon: repressor + operator + promoter (inducible, negative control) · human genome: ~3×10⁹ bp, ~20,000 genes

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Replication needs DNA polymerase, primase, ligase, helicase, and a template; transcription needs RNA polymerase and promoter; translation needs ribosomes (rRNA), tRNA with anticodons, and mRNA. The genetic code is universal, degenerate (multiple codons per amino acid), non-overlapping and commaless — conditions that make it robust to mutation.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: HGP objectives: sequence all ~3 billion base pairs, identify all genes, map variations, and make data public (completed 2003). Adaptive radiation: Darwin's finches (14 species from one ancestor, beak shapes matched to food). Hardy-Weinberg: p²+2pq+q² = 1 — allele frequencies frozen without mutation, selection, migration, drift, or non-random mating.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Central-dogma flow: DNA replication (semiconservative, each new molecule keeps one parental strand) → transcription (mRNA carries the code from nucleus to cytoplasm) → translation (ribosome reads codons, tRNA delivers amino acids, polypeptide folds). Gene regulation example: lac operon OFF when lactose absent (repressor bound); ON when lactose present (inducer removes repressor).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Central dogma has exceptions: reverse transcriptase (retroviruses, RNA→DNA), prions (protein-only inheritance). HGP's 'gene count' (~20,000) surprised everyone (fewer than expected). Hardy-Weinberg describes populations that by definition are NOT evolving — a null model, not reality.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Semiconservative replication derives from complementary base pairing: each strand templates its complement, so daughter molecules must each contain one parental strand — Meselson-Stahl confirmed with ¹⁵N/¹⁴N density gradients. The genetic code's degeneracy (61 sense codons → 20 amino acids) buffers against point mutations; wobble at the third position explains much of it.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: DNA→RNA→protein, with replication as the copy step. Code: 64 = 4³, 61 sense + 3 stop. HGP: sequence + map + function + public (4 objectives). Hardy-Weinberg: p²+2pq+q² = 1, equilibrium means no evolution.

rows.label: Board question
